driver: A recurring wave reaches each group of units at a stable lag behind the group it spreads from while its calendar timing moves from cycle to cycle, so a fixed forward window holds whichever groups' waves fall inside it this cycle; carrying what the same window held in past cycles, or the pool's own history aligned on this cycle's peak, misses a group whose wave has always come after the window and this cycle falls wholly inside it.
driver_concrete: The winter respiratory wave reaches the North's eight hospitals five to six weeks after Metro Detroit's in every winter on the association's capacity census, while its timing moves by weeks from winter to winter; this winter Metro Detroit and West and Central Michigan peaked in mid-December, earlier than in any winter on file, so the four weeks from Monday 4 January 2027 hold none of the sixteen southern hospitals' surge days and the whole of the North's, whose eight hospitals join the pool this winter and whose wave fell in February or March in every earlier winter; the block is the North's own per-wave surge-day draw at its surge plans' agency staffing, 600 shifts.
stump: Averaging the closed winters' January block draws, the sixteen southern members' surge nights in those four weeks at their surge plans' agency staffing with the North's none, files 2,850 shifts; the step that lands it there is reading January by the calendar when the respiratory wave's timing moves by weeks from winter to winter and reaches the North five to six weeks after the Southeast, so this January, after the south peaked in December, holds the North's whole wave and none of the south's: 600 shifts.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who stitches the capacity census's two layouts, reads the pool agreement and the surge plan register correctly and averages the closed winters' January block draws at the register's staffing files 2,850 shifts against the golden 600 (the analyst who sees the early peak and carries the pool's own weeks after each closed winter's peak files none); only timing the North's wave by its lag behind the Southeast puts its whole wave and none of the south's in the block weeks (executed in checks.py on the generator's clean truth and on the pack).
domain_test: The deciding quantity is each region's January surge staffing demand, forecast the way health-system capacity planners forecast a winter surge: by where each region's respiratory wave falls in the window, timed from the region it spreads from by the lag past winters show, and turned into agency shifts through each hospital's surge unit staffing; with another field's nouns (megawatt-hours, crew hours) there is no epidemic travelling from region to region at a lag of weeks, no surge plan opening agency-staffed beds and no reason one region's whole demand should fall in a window it has never touched.
